parsed.explanation: Parent regime creates a known traveler-facing exposure: X passports no longer issued, entry officers instructed to refuse on document discrepancy and consider fraud consequences, and federal birth-sex facility restrictions, with harmful federal custody practices documented, though several measures are litigated or enjoined. The division mitigates this materially: no mapped facility ban, public-accommodation anti-discrimination law covering hotels and transport with a complaint body able to grant relief, bias-crime enhancements, privacy protections, and a healthcare-access order expressly covering travelers. No complaint-outcome, prosecution, or trans-specific violence-rate statistics are documented, so working enforcement and violence safety remain uncertain; the per-capita killing dataset gives no usable rate or background comparison. Overall, strong state protections offset, but do not erase, national document, facility, and custody exposure.
